tested_law: On 5x3-k3 T2-O states, retain exact rank and the frozen component-parity variables; decode relative W/D/L in GF(2)^2 using a rank-specific affine polynomial of degree at most two.

findings.statement: The full observed exact-rank quadratic GF(2)^2 model is consistent on the complete 5x3-k3 T2-O carrier: 7,255 equations, zero contradictions.

The degree-1 submodel exactly reproduces the prior 18 contradictions before quadratic terms are enabled. The degree-2 pass therefore does not arise from a changed component producer, T2 rule, rank convention, or outcome encoding.
No refinement of the tested scalar Q was required. Holding exact-rank component parity plus T2 fixed and enlarging only D from affine to quadratic resolves the complete 5x3-k3 nonadditivity set.

The existence proof is highly nonminimal: the quadratic system exposes 2,104 observed pair variables in addition to 3,276 linear variables and 15 rank offsets, with active nullity 2,135. This is evidence for a degree bound in this carrier, not yet a simple structural evaluator.

The degree-2 success is consistent with the preceding certificate family: every minimum affine obstruction is a four-row rectangle with a size-two local substitution, exactly the discrete-derivative shape that quadratic interaction terms can absorb.

The same frozen exact-rank degree-2 model class must be tested on 4x4-k4, the independent carrier retaining 168 degree-1 contradictions, before quadratic composition is treated as a cross-geometry candidate.

nonclaims: This does not prove pairwise interactions are minimal.
This does not provide a closed-form component-interaction valuation.
This does not establish quadratic sufficiency on 4x4-k4 or any larger geometry.
next_question: Does the identical exact-rank degree-2 GF(2)^2 model class eliminate the 168 independent affine contradictions on complete 4x4-k4?
